stories.headline: Anthropic Finalizes $1.5B Joint Venture With Blackstone, Goldman Sachs to Sell AI to PE Portfolios

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is finalizing an approximately $1.5 billion joint venture with Blackstone, Goldman Sachs, Hellman & Friedman, and General Atlantic to sell AI tools to private-equity-backed companies.
Anthropic, Blackstone, and Hellman & Friedman are each expected to invest roughly $300 million; Goldman Sachs is set to invest around $150 million as a founding investor.
The venture will operate as a consulting and deployment arm, helping PE portfolio companies integrate Claude across operations in areas like finance, customer service, and analytics.
OpenAI announced a similar but larger joint venture, DeployCo, anchored by TPG, Bain Capital, Advent International, Brookfield, and Goanna Capital with about $4 billion committed.
Goldman Sachs has been piloting Claude internally for autonomous agents in accounting and compliance, with embedded Anthropic engineers reportedly spending six months inside the bank.

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Security Public Beta for Enterprise Vulnerability Scanning

key_facts.fact: Anthropic announced the public beta of Claude Security, a cybersecurity tool that scans codebases, detects vulnerabilities, and generates patches, powered by Claude Opus 4.7.
Claude Security can scan full enterprise repositories and open Claude Code to fix vulnerabilities in a single session, with one-click scanning that analyzes component relationships and data usage.
The tool attaches a confidence percentage to each finding to reduce false positives, and now includes scheduled and targeted scans plus export to Slack, Jira, CSV, and Markdown.
Claude Security was previously known as Claude Code Security, first made available to select organizations as a research preview; it is now accessible within Claude or via a dedicated website page.
The launch follows the UK AI Security Institute's independent verification that Anthropic's Mythos Preview was the first model to complete a 32-step enterprise network attack simulation.

stories.headline: Cerebras Targets Up to $40B Valuation in IPO, Kicks Off Roadshow Monday

key_facts.fact: Cerebras is scheduled to start its IPO roadshow on Monday with shares priced between $115 and $125, listing on Nasdaq under ticker 'CBRS'.
Bloomberg reported Cerebras could raise up to $4 billion, targeting a valuation of around $40 billion, making it one of the largest AI chip listings to date.
Cerebras revenue rose to $510 million in 2025, up from $290.3 million the prior year, and reported profit of $1.38 per share, a turnaround from a loss of $9.90 per share.
This is Cerebras' second attempt to go public after withdrawing a previous IPO filing last October.
Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Barclays, and UBS are the lead underwriters for the offering.

stories.headline: EU's €20B AI Gigafactory Plan Faces Criticism Over Demand Doubts and Nvidia GPU Dependency

key_facts.fact: European Commission plans €20 billion for 4-5 AI gigafactories with 100,000+ GPUs each, forming Europe's answer to OpenAI's $500B Stargate project
76 bids for 60 sites across 16 countries were filed, but legislators and experts question whether actual demand exists for the compute capacity
A group of 18 European Parliament lawmakers warned the Commission about dependency on Nvidia as a single chip supplier, questioning how the plan reduces strategic dependencies
Mistral is not waiting for gigafactories: announced $1.2B data center in Sweden in February and raised hundreds of millions for a Paris facility in March
Commission defended plan as about 'sovereign compute' with data 'fully protected under European law, without the possibility of third country interference'
Siemens warned EU regulations are pushing its AI spending outside Europe; financing model requires 65% from private parties, already causing delays

stories.headline: Five Eyes Intelligence Alliance Publishes Joint Guidance Warning Against Rapid Agentic AI Adoption

key_facts.fact: CISA, NSA, and cybersecurity agencies from the UK, Australia, Canada, and New Zealand co-authored guidance titled 'Careful adoption of agentic AI services' published on Friday May 2.
The document lists 23 different risks and over 100 individual best practices, warning that every component in an agentic AI system widens the attack surface.
The agencies warn organizations should 'assume that agentic AI systems may behave unexpectedly' and prioritize 'resilience, reversibility and risk containment over efficiency gains.'
The guidance recommends organizations should 'never grant broad or unrestricted access, especially to sensitive data' and 'only use agentic AI for low-risk and non-sensitive tasks.'
The agencies note that threat intelligence for agentic AI is still evolving, with OWASP and MITRE ATLAS currently focused on LLMs, leaving some attack vectors unique to agentic AI unaddressed.

stories.headline: GameStop Makes Unsolicited ~$56B Offer to Buy eBay, Cohen Ready to Go Hostile

key_facts.fact: GameStop proposed on Sunday to buy eBay for ~$56B at $125/share in a 50-50 cash-and-stock deal, a 20% premium to eBay's Friday close
GameStop has built a ~5% stake in eBay and secured a $20B commitment letter from TD Bank for debt financing
GameStop had ~$9.4B in cash as of January 31; the company's market cap was ~$12B vs eBay's ~$46B, making it a dramatic reverse-scale acquisition
Cohen said he would pursue a proxy fight if eBay's board is unreceptive, and aims to cut $2B of eBay's annualized costs within 12 months
Cohen told WSJ he wants to make eBay 'a legit competitor to Amazon' and is 'thinking about turning eBay into something worth hundreds of billions of dollars'

stories.headline: China's Linkerbot Closes $3B Series B+, Targets $6B With 80%+ Global Robotic Hands Share

key_facts.fact: Beijing-based Linkerbot completed a 'Series B+' funding round last week valued at $3 billion, and will seek $6 billion in its next round
Linkerbot holds over 80% of the global market share in high-degree-of-freedom (DoF) robotic hands, the only firm shipping above 1,000 units per month
Plans to scale production from roughly 5,000 units per month to 10,000 units per month
Early backers include Alibaba's Ant Group and Sequoia spin-off HongShan Group; latest round added Zhongguancun Science Park Fund, Bank of China Asset Management, and Fosun Capital
Two-year-old company with 400+ employees and five factories across Beijing and Shenzhen, some designed as intelligent production lines where robotic hands assemble more robotic hands
Linkerbot's hands can rapidly turn screws, grasp deformable soft objects, thread a needle, and perform high-precision manufacturing, with a 500+ dexterous skill dataset called LinkerSkillNet
Humanoid robot costs remain $100K-$150K per unit for leading industrial models from Unitree, AgiBot, and UBTech; Unitree filed for Shanghai IPO in March at up to $7B valuation

stories.headline: Nvidia's Asian Suppliers Now ~90% of Production Costs, Up From 65%, as Ties Shift to Physical AI

key_facts.fact: Asian suppliers account for about 90% of Nvidia's production costs, up from roughly 65% last year, according to Bloomberg data
In the past week alone, LG Electronics, Nanya Technology, Desay SV, and Pateo Connect rallied on news of Nvidia tie-ups, supply-chain participation, or product collaboration
Latest wave of collaborations shifts beyond semiconductors into physical AI, including robotics, autonomous systems, and AI-enabled manufacturing
Nvidia accounts for roughly half of Microsoft's capex and about one-quarter of Amazon's, with a smaller but still leading share at Meta and Alphabet
Core partnerships deepened through chip-focused ties with TSMC, SK Hynix, and Samsung; hyperscalers committed $190B-$200B each in 2026 capex (Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet) and up to $145B (Meta)

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Says China AI Accelerator Market Share Has 'Dropped to Zero,' Calls Export Policy Backfire

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang told the Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP) that Nvidia's market share of AI accelerators in China has 'now dropped to zero'
Huang said US export policy 'has already largely backfired' and called for policy to be 'dynamically adjusted'
An estimated $1 billion worth of Nvidia chips are being smuggled into China per quarter
Bernstein had projected Nvidia's China AI chip market share would fall from 66% in 2024 to ~8% in 2026, but Huang says the actual decline is steeper
Huang argued it is strategically unsound to abandon a market as large as China and said keeping US chip companies in that market 'is very meaningful'

stories.headline: Jensen Huang Says Nvidia's China AI Chip Market Share Has Dropped to Zero

key_facts.fact: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the company's market share of AI accelerators in China has 'now dropped to zero' in an interview with the Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP).
Huang said US export policy 'has already largely backfired' and that abandoning a market the size of China is strategically unwise.
Bernstein earlier predicted Nvidia's China AI GPU share could fall from 66% in 2024 to about 8%; the actual decline to zero was far steeper than expected.
Some estimates suggest roughly $1 billion worth of Nvidia chips are being smuggled into China per quarter.

Huang acknowledged China remains a formidable AI competitor even without advanced US GPUs, citing its cheaper energy, massive talent pool of scientists and mathematicians, and growing domestic hardware alternatives.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Says China AI Chip Market Share Dropped to Zero; US Senator Demands H200 Export Answers

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang told SCSP that Nvidia's market share of AI accelerators in China has 'now dropped to zero', down from 95% before export controls began
Huang said US export policy 'has already largely backfired' and called abandoning a market the size of China strategically unsound
Sen. Chris Coons pressed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about contradictions regarding H200 chip sales to China in a letter reported May 3

Lutnick told April 22 hearing 'We have not sold them any chips as of yet,' contradicting Huang's March statement that Nvidia got approvals from both US and Chinese governments to sell H200 chips to China
Bernstein had predicted Nvidia's China AI GPU share would drop from 66% in 2024 to ~8%, but actual decline was far more dramatic according to Huang
Huawei's AI chip market share in China now exceeds 50%, with projections of 60% growth in 2026, filling the void Nvidia left
Coons asked Lutnick to respond within one week with how many H200 chips received export licenses, how many shipped, and how many more the Commerce Department plans to license

stories.headline: OPEC+ Agrees to Raise June Oil Output by 188,000 Barrels per Day After UAE Exit

key_facts.fact: Seven OPEC+ countries — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman — agreed on May 3 to increase production by 188,000 barrels per day in June
June output quotas set at 10.291M bpd for Saudi Arabia and 9.762M bpd for Russia, not including compensation for overproduction
The increase aims to accelerate compensation for overproduction since January 2024, following the UAE's withdrawal from OPEC+
US national average gas price hit $4.45/gallon, up from $2.98 before the Iran war began, after surging ~30 cents in the prior week
US Treasury Secretary Bessent said oil prices could start declining within 3 to 9 months, citing the UAE's OPEC exit and oil tankers stranded in the Gulf

stories.headline: SoftBank Plans to Produce Lithium- and Cobalt-Free Data Center Batteries in Japan by FY2027

key_facts.fact: SoftBank Group will seek to make batteries that do not require expensive lithium and cobalt in Japan, targeting production as soon as FY2027
The initiative is part of Japan's broader push to reduce reliance on Chinese-controlled metal supply chains for critical minerals
Batteries are intended for data center use, connecting SoftBank's energy strategy to its AI infrastructure ambitions including the $33B Piketon power plant and $500B Stargate partnership

stories.headline: Trump Launches 'Project Freedom' to Escort Ships From Strait of Hormuz as Iran Sends 14-Point Plan

key_facts.fact: Trump announced 'Project Freedom' starting Monday to help stranded ships leave the Strait of Hormuz, calling it a humanitarian gesture for 'neutral and innocent' countries
Iran sent a 14-point counterproposal via Pakistan calling for nonaggression guarantees, sanctions relief, lifting the naval blockade, and ending the war 'on all fronts' including Lebanon
Trump expressed doubt the proposal would be acceptable, saying Iran 'has not yet paid a big enough price for what they have done to humanity, and the world, over the last 47 years'
The IRGC Navy likely attacked a vessel 11 nautical miles west of Sirik on May 3, the latest in at least two dozen attacks since the war began
The IRGC said it is on standby for a return to war, saying a resumption of hostilities is 'likely' as evidence shows the US 'is not committed to any agreements or treaties'
Iran's proposal includes a three-phase plan: end the war within 30 days in Phase 1, delay nuclear talks to Phase 2, with Iran offering to discuss pausing uranium enrichment for up to 15 years

stories.headline: Ukraine Strikes Russia's Primorsk Port, Sinks Missile Ship, and Hits 3 Shadow Fleet Oil Tankers

key_facts.fact: Ukraine struck a Karakurt-class missile ship (equipped with Kalibr cruise missile launchers and 8 missiles with 2,000 km range), a patrol boat, and a shadow fleet tanker at Primorsk port on May 3
Two more shadow fleet tankers were hit near the entrance to Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiysk using unmanned surface vessels
Primorsk, Russia's largest oil exporting port on the Baltic Sea, lies over 1,000 km from Ukraine between the Russian-Finnish border and St. Petersburg
Satellite imagery shows Ukraine's late-April strikes on the Transeft Perm dispatch station burned ~70% of the facility and destroyed all 50,000 cubic meter tanks, halting operations
Russia deployed a record 6,583 long-range drones in April, surpassing March's previous high, averaging over 200 per day
Zelenskyy said Russia has lost at least $7 billion this year from attacks on its oil sector, with exports from Ust-Luga and Primorsk declining

stories.headline: xAI Quietly Releases Grok 4.3 With Always-On Reasoning and $1.25/M Token Pricing

key_facts.fact: xAI released Grok 4.3 quietly with no press release, featuring always-on reasoning that cannot be toggled off, a 1M-token context window, and uncapped output length.
Grok 4.3 is priced at $1.25/$2.50 per million input/output tokens, reducing overall running costs by approximately 20% compared to Grok 4.20 according to Artificial Analysis estimates.
The model matches the scale of Grok 4.20 including its 16-agent Heavy system, with an improved architecture and a December 2025 knowledge cutoff.
The model adds native video understanding and the ability to generate structured documents like slides, PDFs, and spreadsheets directly in conversation.
On the Intelligence Index, Grok 4.3 now sits just above Muse Spark and Claude Sonnet 4.6.

stories.headline: Xiaomi Releases MiMo-V2.5-Pro, a 1T-Parameter Open-Weight Model Rivaling Claude Opus on Coding

key_facts.fact: MiMo-V2.5-Pro is a mixture-of-experts model with 1.02 trillion total parameters and 42 billion active per request, with a 1 million token context window.
The model built a complete compiler from a Peking University course in 4.3 hours across 672 tool calls, scoring 233 out of 233 on the hidden test suite.
On SWE-bench Verified it scores 78.9%, on SWE-Bench Pro 57.2%, and on Terminal-Bench 2.0 68.4%, placing it close to Claude Opus 4.6 (77.1 on MiMo Coding Bench).
Xiaomi claims MiMo-V2.5-Pro uses 40 to 60 percent fewer tokens than Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4 on equivalent agent tasks.
In a second demo, MiMo-V2.5-Pro wrote a desktop video editor with roughly 8,000 lines of code running autonomously for 11.5 hours and making about 1,870 tool calls.
